newsitem.title: Australia: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: PM SAYS BRINGING DOWN UNEMPLOYMENT SHOULD BE MAJOR GOAL
The Prime Minister says he warmly welcomes the importance the Governor of the Reserve Bank, Ian McFarlane, has placed on bringing down unemployment.
In a Melbourne speech last night, Mr McFarlane said wage outcomes and unemployment remained the bank's immediate focus.
He said Australia must review every policy and practice it has in place in a bid to bring down jobless levels.
John Howard says reducing unemployment should remain Australia's principal social objective, and is a goal of his Government.
PM DENIES HE'S REBUFFED COSTELLO
The Prime Minister has denied suggestions that he's rebuffed Treasurer Peter Costello by saying he doesn't want an early election.
Mr Howard has backed up Mr Costello's warning that the Government will re-submit to the Senate a rejected bill dealing with new migrants' acccess to welfare.

The Prime Minister has stressed the Government will do what it can to get its legislation through, but says people shouldn't infer from the Treasurer's statement that the Government is angling for an early election.
DECISION RESERVED ON MURDER APPEAL
The New South Wales Supreme Court has reserved its judgement on whether murderer Andrew Kalajzich should have his life sentence replaced with a set term.
The former millionaire businessman has already spent ten years in jail for hiring contract killers to murder his wife Megan at their Fairlight home in January, 1986.
He applied to the Supreme Court today for minimum and maximum terms to the set under the Truth in Sentencing laws.
His counsel told the court Kalajzich hoped to join his son in business upon his release.
It was claimed the murder was not in the most serious category of a multiple killing, thrill killing or sex-related attack.
BRYANT WILL SUFFER MORE MENTAL PROBLEMS: PSYCHIATRIST
A Melbourne forensic psychiatrist predicts the Port Arthur gunman, Martin Bryant, will become more difficult to manage as his solitary confinement drags on.
Tim Watson-Munroe says Bryant is likely to suffer more mental problems through being kept in indefinite solitary confinement, and that will reduce his ability to cope.
But Mr watson-Munroe says Tasmanian prison authorities have little choice but to keep him segregated from other inmates.
He says while Bryant told detectives interviewing him about the massacre he wanted to mix with other prisoners, that would not be a good idea.
He says a prisoner who killed somebody who has murdered 35 people would gain a deal of stature in the prison sub-culture.
MINISTER APPEALS TO MINERS TO END STRIKE
New South Wales Treasurer, Michael Egan, has appealed to striking coal miners to return to work, and for the opposition to realise it's made a mistake over compenstaion for them.
Mine workers went out indefinately last night when the Opposition moved to include them in a reduced benefits in the general workers compensation scheme.
Mr Egan says the government is ready to recall parliament to allow the opposition to vote down its amendments.
He says the stoppage will cost the state more than twelve-million dollars a day in exports.

The Minerals Council says it lobbied the Opposition to alter the benefits and the Government failed to consult with it. Industrial Relations minister, Jeff Shaw, will take proposals to Cabinet on Monday which may resolve the dispute.
KEMP SAYS FUNDING FOR STUDENTS WHO DON'T GO ON TO UNI

Federal Education Minister David Kemp, says additional funding for vocational education in Australia's schools, is being directed at the 60 per cent of students who don't go on to full time tertiary study.
Dr Kemp today announced 20 million dollars funding for vocational education in schools around the country.

New South Wales will get 5.9 million, Victoria 4.6 million, Queensland 3.5 million, Western Australia 2.1 million, South Australia 1.7 million, Tasmania 795-thousand, ACT 644-thousand and Northern Territory 520-thousand.
Dr Kemp says the idea is to ensure that those students who don't go on to tertiary study after school, pick up skills which will stand them in good stead.
INVESTIGATIONS INTO SURF LIFESAVING COLLAPSE
Police, Surf Lifesaving and local authorities are investigating the collapse of a Gold Coast clubhouse balcony which injured three New South Wales visitors.
The men from Tuggerah were taken to hospital after the balcony of the Broadbeach surf lifesaving club fell four metres to the ground.
The men were supervising 35 youths believed to be part of a blue light disco contingent.
Surf Life Saving Queensland general manager, Brett Williamson, says the prioritites are the injured men and the safety of the building.
ROSE WINS FIRST ROUND
The widow of the late mining magnate Lang Hancock, has won the latest round in the battle with her step-daughter over control of her late husband's multi-million dollar fortune.

The Supreme Court in Perth has allowed Rose Porteous to proceed with legal action against Mr Hancock's daughter, Gina Rinehart, who she has accused of conspiring to cheat and defraud her out of her rightful inheritance.
Mrs Rinehart had applied to the Court to have the legal action against her struck out, claiming it was an abuse of the Court process, embarrassing and vexatious.
However, today Supreme Court Master Bredmeyer dismissed Mrs Rinehart's application meaning Mrs Porteous' action can continue.
The matter will proceed to a further hearing where Mrs Porteous will argue that she's been deprived of her entitlements to her late husband's estate.
Mrs Porteous has further alleged Mrs Rinehart and others devised a plan, which included a break-in to an office, as part of a conspiracy against her.
